title: Telemetry ingest preprocessor: schema enforcement, PII scrub, and adaptive sink routing
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Our current log/event ingestion accepts heterogeneous JSON events from many services. This causes index explosion in Loki/ES, inconsistent correlation id placement, accidental PII leakage, and operational burden when routing tenants to different retention/compute backends.

Proposal: Implement a light-weight telemetry preprocessor service that runs as an ingest sidecar / central gateway shim to: 1) validate/normalize event schema against a small canonical shape per event-type, 2) hydrate missing trace/span/correlation fields from headers or sampled traces, 3) apply PII scrubbing policies and field redaction based on tenant-level policy, 4) canonicalize high-cardinality keys, 5) route events to the correct sink (Loki for structured logs, ES for long-term indexing, s3 for raw archive) based on tenant configuration, event type, and retention tier, and 6) provide backpressure and retry semantics for downstream outages with buffered durable writes for burst spikes.

Goals: reduce index cardinality by 40% for high-volume services, eliminate >90% of accidental PII fields in stored indexes, ensure every log line has either trace_id or correlation_id (or a generated sampling marker), and provide a migration path for tenants to opt into structured schema enforcement with minimal producer changes.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Preprocessor runs in front of 3 pilot services and normalizes their event payloads without dropping critical fields.
2) Dashboard shows per-tenant cardinality delta and overall index size reduction >= 25% in staging after 2 weeks of traffic.
3) PII fuzz tests pass: common PII patterns (emails, credit card numbers) are removed/redacted in stored sinks for pilot tenants.
4) All events in sinks have a top-level correlation key (trace_id|corr_id|generated_marker).
5) Fail-open policy verified: when preprocessor is degraded, events are forwarded raw to a quarantine topic and alerts fire; no client-facing latency impact beyond 50ms p95.
6) Runbook documented and on-call trained for two weeks before wider rollout.
notes:
Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Telemetry+Preprocessor+Design (v2). Prototype implemented in Go using a plugin-based validator (jsonschema + custom rule hooks). Considerations: 1) Do we mutate incoming event structure or attach a normalized envelope? Mutating reduces downstream mapping but increases migration risk; envelope approach is safer for initial rollout. 2) Where to run the component: sidecar vs central gateway vs managed collector. Plan is hybrid: sidecar for high-volume internal services, central gateway for public ingestion. 3) Performance: aim for <2ms median add-on latency for small events; use pre-allocated buffers and fast-path for events already compliant. 4) Privacy: PII rules must be configurable at tenant granularity and audited via generated sample events.

Trade-offs: Inline PII scrubbing reduces stored sensitive data but complicates debugging; therefore raw archives to s3 (encrypted + limited access) will be retained for 30 days for legal/debugging with stricter access controls. Using jsonschema for validation is fast to get started but will need custom rule engine for canonicalization and high-cardinality bucketization.

Rollout plan: 1) Spike + bench (2 weeks) -> 2) Pilot (3 tenants, 4 services) in staging (2 weeks) -> 3) Canary in prod for 1 engineering org with monitoring and automated rollback (3 weeks) -> 4) Gradual opt-in and cluster-wide deployment with console controls to toggle enforcement and retention policies.
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Ticket opened after observability guild spike highlighted 3 services with high index cardinality and inconsistent trace IDs.

2026-02-25: Spike complete — lightweight Go preprocessor prototype accepts events, runs jsonschema, and outputs canonical envelope. Bench: ~1.8ms median added latency on c6i-type boxes. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-preprocessor/pull/23
2026-03-03: Security did initial review of PII patterns and recommended tenant-scoped regex allowlist + audit logging. Decided to keep raw archival with tighter ACLs.
2026-03-05: Implemented sink-routing rules — mappings for Loki vs ES vs S3. Discovered high-cardinality map keys from 'user_context' requiring bucketing heuristics.
2026-03-09: Integration tests against staging Loki cluster passed for schema enforcement flows; ES mapping tests show mapping explosion for nested maps — plan to flatten and hash keys.
2026-03-12: Started pilot onboarding for payments and auth services. Found rate-limit backpressure path needs a durable queue for spikes — evaluating Redis Streams vs Kafka topic per-tenant.
